title: Log Fabric: schema-first routing and reliable correlation ID propagation to Loki + ELK
creator: Samir Desai
description:
Problem: As Redwood scales, our service logs are high-cardinality, variably structured, and produced by many languages/runtimes. Downstream teams (SRE, Runtime, Console) need: reliable correlation between traces and logs, consistent structured fields across sinks, low-latency delivery to Loki for real-time debugging, and searchable indexing in ELK for long-term analytics. Current producers emit heterogeneous JSON or plaintext; some libs drop trace/request IDs or use different keys (trace_id / x-request-id / reqId).

Goal: Build a 'log fabric' — a schema-first ingestion router and transformation layer that:
- Normalizes incoming logs to a platform schema (common fields, types, and canonical correlation ids)
- Propagates or synthesizes correlation IDs consistently and enriches logs with trace metadata when available
- Routes enriched logs to appropriate sinks (Loki for live tailing, Elasticsearch for historics) with sink-specific adaptations (labels/indices, chunking/size limits)
- Supports tenant-aware routing, redaction rules, and backpressure handling when downstream queues saturate
- Emits observability around the fabric itself (lag, error rates, transform CPU, accepted/rejected counts)

Scope: Implement core pipeline components (ingester, transformer workers, router, sink adapters) and a migration plan for top 12 log producers. Exclude full replacement of legacy sidecar shims in this ticket — those will be incremental migration tasks.
acceptance_criteria: Ingest API accepts ndjson/structured JSON and plaintext with heuristics and returns 200/accepted-along-with-uuid
Pipeline normalizes to platform schema (timestamp, level, service, environment, trace_id, span_id, request_id, message, attrs) for >=95% of incoming structured logs
Missing correlation IDs are synthesized deterministically and tagged as synthesized: true
Transformer enriches logs with trace tags via Trace Lookup API (when trace_id present) without adding >10ms p50 per-log overhead
Loki sink receives logs with required label set and shows <30s to first-appear in live tail for 99th percentile under target load
ELK sink indexes logs with platform fields and searchable mapping; no mapping explosions for top-traffic namespaces
Backpressure behavior defined and exercised: when Kafka consumer lag > threshold, ingester returns 429 with retry-after and emits metrics
Automated migration runbooks exist for top-12 producers and at least 3 producer migrations completed in-canary with rollout plan
Dashboards created: Log Fabric Health (lag, error-rate, transformer latency), Correlation Coverage (percent logs with trace_id), Sink Delivery SLA metrics
